# Frozen revision 9 song-body loudness measurements

This oracle calls the unchanged `pyloudnorm 0.1.1` default `Meter(32000).integrated_loudness` used by accepted `session_render.render_song`. It measures stereo Float32 input with a fresh filter state. The input is already the chosen song-body slice; it does not warm the meter with the preceding intro. This primitive applies no gain, peak protection, rack scheduling, or mastering. It targets the accepted library's default K weighting, including its rounding behavior, rather than substituting another implementation of a loudness standard.

The high shelf runs first, then the high pass. Each SciPy filter uses Double coefficients and state, and assignment back to the Float32 input copy rounds after each filter. For each 400 ms block, squaring, the contiguous NumPy sum, and multiplication by the reciprocal of 12,800 are Float32 operations under pinned NumPy 2.3.5. Block energies are then stored as Double. Blocks overlap by 75%; an incomplete last block keeps the denominator 12,800. The initial gate includes blocks at or above −70 LUFS; the final gate requires strictly greater than both −70 and the relative threshold. The relative threshold is 10 LU below the first gated mean. Silence or a wholly gated signal produces original negative infinity, represented by `measurable: false` and `lufs: 0` in the native transport contract.

The original block-count expression evaluates duration in Double and rounds with ties to even. It is not equivalent to rounding an exact rational frame count: 24,000 frames produces four blocks and 59,200 produces sixteen. The manifest freezes every half-hop count across the supported 12,800–5,792,000-frame range. It also records that all original lower/upper endpoint calculations for block indices 0–1,807 equal exact multiples of 3,200. Source hashes and exact Double filter coefficients identify the pinned dependency. Per-case diagnostics retain filtered probes, all block energies, gate membership, and the relative threshold as independent debugging evidence.

Seventeen cases cover minimum-length silence and stereo impulses, 25 Hz and 8 kHz square waves, unequal channels and changing channel activity, floating half-hop boundaries, partial final windows, absolute-gate margins of approximately ±0.001 LU, relative gating, maximum supported duration, and an original musical body excerpt. Procedural `input_segments` overwrite a zero stereo input in listed order. A segment repeats its Float32 `pattern`, holding each entry for `hold_frames`; its pattern index is `((frame-start)/hold_frames) % pattern.count` with integer division. No native RNG, trigonometry, or amplitude calculation constructs these inputs.

The 32,000-frame musical input is the first second of the accepted first song's body, beginning at frame 393,846. Freezing and verification regenerate all 621 original events over the original 3,711,911 frames before cropping. The complete original body ends at frame 3,150,769; its independently measured scalar and gate counts are recorded separately. The checked-in excerpt is read exactly by both meters, with fresh K-filter state, so waveform differences elsewhere in the native full-song implementation cannot be confused with meter error. The known native/original full-song event-duration discrepancy remains a separate diagnostic and is not accepted or changed by this fixture.

The acceptance limit was fixed before native comparison: finite integrated loudness must differ by at most `1e-5` LU, while input frames, total blocks, both gate counts, and measurable status must match exactly. All candidate fields are checked, including finite scalar values and the zero sentinel for an unmeasurable result. Every native JSON filename must be present exactly once, with no additional files. Original reference regeneration must retain the frozen gate membership and scalar limit. Full-stream hashes identify the freezing platform; the regenerated musical excerpt may differ by at most `2e-7` in sample amplitude across pinned platforms. The native meter always receives the exact frozen excerpt. Existing audio goldens and their tolerances remain unchanged.

`freeze-loudness.py` refuses to replace an existing fixture without explicit `--replace` and never runs in CI. `verify-loudness.py --compare .build/tonal-native/loudness --evidence .build/tonal-evidence/loudness` regenerates the original measurements and writes scalar/count comparison evidence and hashes. This analysis-only primitive does not produce new listening WAVs. No Python package or developer fixture enters the app bundle.
